quizName: Hardest Questions in Arkansas Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You like, without thinking about other riders.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best and where you have space around your motorcycle. The best lane position changes based on road conditions. A good rider adjusts their position as needed.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What should be your first consideration when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay together while keeping safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Your footwear should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly to speed changes and turns. Slow down earlier when stopping and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good quality, properly-fitted helmet is the most effective thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible while riding, day or night. Reflective clothing also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Your eyes need shadows and light to judge distance. At night, artificial lights distort or hide these visual clues.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Immediately take it on the highway.
Learn where all controls are in a safe area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn where all controls are in a safe area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding in a safe, controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. Stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the rider and hold firmly to the rider's waist or hips. They can also hold handlegrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: White signs with red and black markings show traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before riding. Test both brakes to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: If you must ride on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
Look for dark clouds that signal bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
questions.explanation: Always watch your mirrors to see if drivers behind you are paying attention to you. This helps you know if they are responding to your stop.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are weak.
May hurt your riding ability and requires caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hurt your riding ability and requires caution.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter and prescription medications have side effects that can impair your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Your helmet protects you best when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle. Wear it even when the weather is warm.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.explanation: Good motorcycle clothing protects you in a crash. It also keeps you comfortable and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should be most concerned about the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move your position in the lane to be as visible as possible to other drivers.
